conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed throughout the tested-field, spectral, and rate-model deductions; draft supplier status does not constitute proof acceptance.

The reduced branch uses length parameter u, inverse-length κ, lower-boundary covariance Cκ, and the negative-sign angular Fourier transform. Its frequency argument is E/(ℏc); the acceleration branch uses proper seconds and frequency E/ℏ.
Both branches adopt positive rates and the equation p′=r↑(1−p)−r↓p with p(0)∈[0,1]. These rates are model inputs, not exact QFT transition probabilities or measured outcomes.

The reduced horizon interpretation requires the same normalized Killing generator and ∇χχ=κχ on a supplied smooth null hypersurface. The local-temperature clause additionally requires a connected stationary bath, lapse one at the reference event, and an explicit reference-temperature match.

Rindler calculations use signature (−,+,+,+), x⁰=ct, W_R={x¹>|x⁰|}, χκ=κ(x¹∂₀+x⁰∂₁), N=κρ, and proper acceleration c²/ρ. Positive generator rescaling changes N and the reference temperature together, leaving local effective temperatures invariant.
The switched estimate requires a nonzero real compactly supported smooth switch and positive duration; it bounds a leading coefficient, not an all-order detector probability.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts two distinct effective branches, their specified spectral rates, and p′(t)=r↑(1−p(t))−r↓p(t), with supplied p(0)∈[0,1]; no exact QFT transition probability or observed reading is asserted.

Under Countable Choice and the selected positive-gap reduced rate model, the unique stationary probability is p*=1/(1+exp(2πE/(ℏcκ))) and the effective reference temperature is T_red=ℏcκ/(2πk_B). Horizon and local stationary-bath interpretations require the additional identifications stated in the theorem.

Under Countable Choice and the selected massless acceleration rate model, p*=1/(1+exp(2πcE/(aℏ))) and T_eff=ℏa/(2πck_B). The stated finite-switch coefficient bound holds; on the specified Rindler wedge, T_U(ρ)=ℏc/(2πk_Bρ)=T_K^acc/N.
